_읽는이에게: 이 파일에 적힌 것은 **전부 실제로 있었던 일**이다.
하나라도 꾸며 넣는 순간 이 페이지는 정확히 반대로 작동한다 —
정직함을 보이려던 페이지가 가장 큰 거짓말이 된다.
항목을 추가할 때는 반드시 커밋 해시나 파일 경로로 근거를 댈 수 있어야 한다.
'그런 일이 있었던 것 같다' 는 넣지 않는다.

rejected.why: A museum about Seoul's history, not the railway station.
A bookshop café. The registered name reads as 'Seoraksan' plus one syllable that changes it entirely.
A car campsite inside the park. Correct area, wrong subject.
A hotel branch named after the station.
A noodle restaurant named after the temple. Not the temple.
A mountain whose name contains the word 'maple'. The photograph showed no autumn colour.
Byte-for-byte identical to a photograph we already had under a different name.
Right place, wrong season. The photographs were summer green, and the article was about autumn colour.
Myeongdong Cathedral, not the shopping district. Caught while choosing a lead image for the doctor article.
This was the lead photograph on our glasses article, and its alt text said 'sunglasses'. Enlarged, the dark round objects are folded fans and the rest is hanbok fabric. There is no eyewear in it.

corrected.wrong: We said free subway travel for over-65s applies automatically at the gate.
corrected.right: It requires an application, and short-term visitors are not eligible at all.
corrected.why: We had confused two different things. Palaces and museums genuinely are free for over-65s including foreign visitors; the subway concession is not the same scheme.

corrected.wrong: We said Korea publishes no official list of Muslim-friendly restaurants.
corrected.right: The Korea Tourism Organization publishes one, in four tiers, and keeps it current.
corrected.why: We asserted an absence without checking the obvious place. An absence is a claim like any other and needs the same evidence.

corrected.wrong: We called it 'five palaces' and then listed four palaces plus Jongmyo, which is a shrine.
corrected.right: Added Gyeonghuigung, and marked Jongmyo in the table as not a palace.

corrected.wrong: Airport bus fares contradicted the figures in another article on this site.
corrected.right: Unified to route-level fares in both.

corrected.wrong: The opening paragraph said two palaces close on Mondays and two on Tuesdays. The table directly below it said otherwise.
corrected.right: Rewrote the paragraph to match the table.
corrected.why: We had corrected the table and not re-read the sentence introducing it. Fixing one element and leaving its neighbour stale is our most common failure.

corrected.wrong: Every page declared a canonical address without a trailing slash, while its own breadcrumb data and the live URL both had one.
corrected.right: One address everywhere. Verified: zero mismatches across canonical, hreflang and sitemap.
corrected.why: A regular expression meant to add the slash was written to replace a slash that had already been stripped, so it did nothing at all.

corrected.wrong: A photograph was imported under the name 'night' and captioned as a side street. It is a daytime photograph under a blue sky. A second one was described as a crowded shopping street; it is a shop on a corner.
corrected.right: Both descriptions rewritten to match the photographs. One of the two moved to an article that actually needed it.
corrected.why: We wrote the captions from the file names rather than from the pictures. That is the same mistake as trusting a registered place name, one step further downstream.

withheld.did: Left the row out and said so.
Used the verified Seoul–Busan fare as an upper bound and labelled it as one. A budget that is slightly too large is fine; one that is slightly too small is a problem.

withheld.missing: How many days photochromic lenses take
withheld.did: Said a few days, told you to ask on the day you order, and did not put a number on it.

withheld.missing: City-by-city bloom dates for the coming season
withheld.did: Gave the observed historical pattern and the forecast source instead of inventing a calendar.

withheld.missing: A government tariff for what a non-insured visitor pays
withheld.did: Kept the range, and said plainly in the article that it is the weakest number on the page.

gates.name: no-shared-images
gates.does: Stops the build if two articles use the same photograph.

gates.name: no-duplicate-files
gates.does: Stops the build if two files are byte-identical under different names.

gates.name: photo-sanity
gates.does: Stops the build if a registered place name contains a word that changes what the place is, or if a photograph in use has no record of a human having opened it.

gates.name: content-quality
gates.does: Stops the build on a missing lead image, a missing caption, an over-length title, or too few internal links.

gates.name: Original quote length
gates.does: Stops the build if a quoted Korean sentence runs past 120 characters.
